title: VP Sara’s camp: House discussing no-el in 2028
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo said yesterday that he had received confirmation about ongoing discussions at the House of Representatives about a no-elections scenario in…

blocks.text: November 19, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo said yesterday that he had received confirmation about ongoing discussions at the House of Representatives about a no-elections (no-el) scenario in 2028.
In an interview over Bilyonaryo News Channel, Panelo said there are talks at the House of Representatives about “no-el” in 2028.

Panelo said in one of their recent conversations, he asked the Vice President what would happen in case she is convicted by the Senate impeachment court and be disqualified to run in the 2028 national elections.
Panelo asked Duterte who would take her place as presidential candidate.

“Her only reply to me was, ‘Oh, attorney, we don’t even know if we would reach the 2028 elections because the information I have been receiving is there is a plan for a ‘no-el’ in 2028, whether that’s by term extensions or converting our form of government into parliamentary,’” said Panelo.
“Since there have been such rumors, and after talking to her, I have received confirmation that there are talks in the Lower House about this,” he added.
Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal has warned that the law postponing this year’s barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections could inspire the postponement as well of the 2028 general elections.

Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Garcia earlier dismissed the possibility of “no-election” in 2028, adding that the poll body has already been preparing for the upcoming national elections.
Former VP helpers ‘safe and sound’
Meanwhile, Panelo said with the help of the police, two former members of the Vice President’s household staff have been found, released and are safe.

Panelo said that on Tuesday, “the Vice President, through her legal team and with the assistance of the police, has since facilitated the release of two former household staff members. They are now safe and sound.”
Duterte’s legal team, accompanied by police officers, reportedly fetched them and brought them to a police station where they executed affidavits. The incident was recorded in the police blotter.
“For now, the apparent plan to use these individuals for false testimony against the Vice President has been foiled,” Panelo said.
Earlier, he raised suspicion that the alleged threats made against the two household staff members could be linked to the Marcos administration.
Panelo said they sought the help of the Philippine National Police (PNP) after one of the household helpers reached out to the Vice President and sought her help, asking that they be rescued.

The helpers said that sometime in October, they were recruited by a private individual to work as employees at a resort in Boracay. They were brought to Manila under the pretext of training for the job.
On Nov. 16, their employer reportedly informed them that there were threats to their lives, and that there was also a threat to the employer’s own life because he was reportedly “harboring” them.

“The employer then told them that the threats would be quelled if they executed affidavits, drafts of which were presented to them. According to the two individuals, the affidavits contained false allegations against the Vice President, which they refused to sign,” Panelo said.
This prompted them to seek the help of the Vice President.
“It was later clarified that they were not held in captivity, but they were afraid to leave the employer’s custody due to the supposed threat to their lives,” Panelo said.
